# dsh-proxy-trust
简体中文
`dsh-proxy-trust` lets the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web UI run behind a reverse proxy. It is intended
for deployments where the proxy handles access, such as Cloudflare Access, and DSH remains bound to
a private or loopback address.
The plugin does not replace DSH's connection service. It changes a small set of checks in the runnin
g service, and each change has its own setting. Everything is off by default.
Settings are available under `Settings > Reverse proxy`. You can also edit the plugin entry in the p
rofile's `cordis.patch.yml`.
## Requirements

- DSH `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`
- Node.js 22 or later
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Start the web profile as usual. Values passed with `--trusted-host` continue to work and are combine
d with the hosts configured by this plugin.
## Configuration
Most changes take effect as soon as they are saved. Enabling `ownsHost` affects the next page load,
while changing the extra listener may close and reopen its port.
| Setting | What it does |
| `hosts` | Adds host names that browsers use to reach DSH, such as `app.example` or `app.example:84

43`. These are combined with any `--trusted-host` values. |
| `hostsAny` | Accepts any `Host` value.

The configured host list is ignored, but DSH's Origin and cross-site checks still run. |
| `skipAut
h` | Stops requiring the DSH launch token and session cookie. The URL DSH prints and opens at startu

p no longer carries a token. The proxy in front of DSH becomes the only login layer. |
| `crossSiteN
avigation` | Allows a cross-site top-level `GET` navigation to `/`, `/index.html`, or `/connect`. Fe

tch requests, uploads, other paths, and WebSocket upgrades do not qualify. |
| `crossSiteReferrers`
| Limits cross-site navigation to listed origins, such as `https://team.cloudflareaccess.com`. An em

pty list places no restriction on the referrer. |
| `ownsHost` | Sets `__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost` o
n the page. DSH then exposes features intended for its own machine, such as "Open configuration file

," even when the page uses a proxy or network address. |
| `listenEnabled` | Opens a second TCP list
ener and forwards its connections to DSH's listener. This provides wildcard or network binding witho

ut changing DSH's own bind address. |
| `listenAddress` | Sets the address for the extra listener. E

mpty or `0.0.0.0` means every IPv4 interface; use `::` for IPv6. |
| `listenPort` | Sets the extra l

istener's port. The default is `3081`, and it must differ from DSH's port. |
| `listenAllow` | Lists
the client IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to use the extra listener. An empty list allows ever
y client that can reach the port. A non-empty list with no valid entry allows nobody. |

## Using the extra listener
DSH 0.2.2 refuses wildcard bind addresses such as `0.0.0.0`. The optional listener works around that
restriction with a plain TCP forwarder inside the DSH process. It passes HTTP, WebSocket, and TLS t
raffic through without interpreting it, so DSH still performs its normal Host, Origin, token, and co
gh without interpreting it, so DSH still performs its normal Host, Origin, token, and cookie checks.
There are a few consequences:
- DSH sees forwarded connections as coming from its own listener, usually `127.0.0.1`. The plugin st

ill uses the real client address for `listenAllow` and refusal logs.
- A remote client can send `Hos
t: localhost` through a listener exposed beyond loopback. The Host check alone is therefore not an a

ccess boundary. Use `listenAllow`, a firewall, or an authenticating proxy.
- The listener accepts up

to 512 simultaneous connections.
- An invalid address, a port already in use, or a missing bind per

mission produces a warning. DSH itself keeps running.
- Firewall rules and container port mappings r
emain your responsibility.

## Security
`skipAuth` removes DSH's browser login check. Anyone who can reach an accepted host is treated as si
gned in. When the plugin detects that login is skipped and the instance is reachable beyond localhos
t, it shows a warning in Settings and writes a warning to the DSH log.
For a remotely reachable deployment, use `skipAuth` only when every route to the instance passes thr
ough a proxy that authenticates users. Restrict the listener so clients cannot bypass that proxy. A
loopback-only instance can use the option without becoming remotely accessible. If DSH's token login
is still useful in your deployment, leave `skipAuth` off and use the other settings independently.
`crossSiteNavigation` is deliberately narrow. It only relaxes DSH's cross-site marker for a document
navigation on the three listed paths. The original Host and Origin checks still decide whether the
three listed paths. The original Host and Origin checks still decide whether the request is trusted.
## Compatibility
The plugin wraps private members of DSH's connection service: the trusted-host list, browser authent
ication object, and request trust method. Those members are not part of DSH's public plugin API.
Each hook checks the runtime shape before installing. If a DSH update changes an expected member, th
at feature stays off and the plugin logs a warning instead of stopping DSH. Unloading the plugin res
tores the original objects and methods.
The package currently supports DSH `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`.
